transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Tom Reynolds (Embera Head of Data), Aisha Patel (Embera ML Eng), Mark Chu (Embera Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Discussed cost per token tradeoffs, batching and cache strategies to reduce unit costs, and next steps to run a Dedicated benchmark. Embera is evaluating hosted vs Dedicated; private deployment discussed briefly for compliance.

Topics: per-token pricing, batching, KV/prefix caching, dedicated committed discounts, pilot scope, SOC2/KMS questions.

[00:00] Jared: Hey team, thanks for joining. I'm Jared, account exec at Redwood, this is Priya our SE. How're you all doing?
[00:06] Tom: Good, thanks. Quick note we have 45 minutes, want to focus on cost model because budget is tight.
[00:11] Jared: Totally understood. Aisha, Mark, quick intros?
[00:15] Aisha: Aisha here, ML engineer, building retriever+generator stacks for trading signals. We'll be heavy on context windows, lots of repeated prefixes.
[00:22] Mark: Mark, infra, responsible for VPC connectivity and cost controls.
[00:27] Priya: Great. We'll frame this around three options: Hosted (pay-as-you-go API), Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity), and Private (customer-managed infra/license). We'll walk per-token, batching and caching levers.

[00:40] Tom: Before we jump, budget target: roughly $10k/month for early phase. Can you do that for our expected volume?
[00:47] Jared: Let's unpack volume first. What are you projecting for initial usage?
[00:51] Aisha: We're aiming for 100k inference requests per day. Average generation length ~150 output tokens, prompt + context about 600 tokens, so ~750 tokens per request on average.
[01:03] Jared: Ok, ballpark 75M tokens/month (100k * 750 * 30). At that scale cost matters.
[01:10] Mark: Yeah that's the worry. If hosted per-token costs are high we blow the budget.

[01:15] Priya: Right. A couple of levers: batching reduces per-request overhead, continuous batching can lower GPU amortized overhead by 20-40% depending on latency SLO. Prefix/KV caching can remove repeated prompt tokens entirely for many requests — especially since you said repeated prefixes. That can cut token spend dramatically.
[01:32] Aisha: Our traffic is fairly repetitive — same market context prepended for many calls, maybe 60% of prompt tokens are identical.
[01:38] Jared: Perfect candidate for prefix caching. For Hosted we have automatic prefix caching and intelligent routing, so repeated tokens are often cached and not recomputed; that maps directly to cost savings.
[01:48] Tom: Can you give us numbers, even rough?
[01:52] Priya: Sure. On Hosted, our reference per-token billing is 1) model inference compute cost and 2) platform surcharge. For a medium-sized open model we typically see effective hosted unit cost in our examples of about $0.00008 to $0.0002 per token for generation depending on model and length — with caching that can drop where 60% of prompt tokens are cached. So effective monthly could drop from 75M tokens to ~30M billable tokens.
[02:17] Aisha: So with 30M billable tokens, at say $0.00012/token that's around $3,600/month, which would be in range.
[02:25] Jared: Right, that's why caching matters. Now Dedicated: with a monthly reserved commit you trade up-front capacity for lower per-token compute — roughly 30-50% lower unit compute costs in our experience because you're amortizing fixed GPU instance costs. You also get predictable throughput so batching efficiency improves.
[02:42] Mark: What does a Dedicated commit look like for our size? Any minimums?
[02:46] Priya: Typical starts at a single-GPU reserved pool. For example, a 1xA10 equivalent pool committed monthly gives you X throughput, and cost per token can be ~40% less than hosted on heavy-generation workloads. We can share exact model-specific numbers in the pricing sheet.
[02:58] Tom: And Private?
[03:00] Jared: Private is a different profile: you pay a platform license + infra costs. If you have deep infra commitments or regulatory constraints, it's useful. Unit cost depends entirely on your infra and utilization — with high utilization Private can be cheapest but requires ops and capital.

[03:14] Tom: We're a small infra team; ops overhead is a concern. Likely Hosted or Dedicated to start.
[03:20] Priya: Makes sense. For dedicated pilots we often run a 48-hour benchmark with your sample traffic to measure effective tokens billed, batching benefits, and latency. That will let us produce a cost projection with committed discounts applied.

[03:32] Aisha: Can we talk about batching — you said 20-40% improvements — what's that depend on?
[03:36] Priya: Two levers: request-level batching (grouping many short requests into larger batches) and continuous batching (server side holds a small window to assemble batches). For lots of short requests, batching reduces per-request kernel launch overhead. The % gain depends on request length distribution and SLO. For example, if most calls are short (<=100 tokens), batching gets you the most. If calls are long, the gain is smaller but overall throughput is better.
[03:56] Mark: Latency SLOs are 200-300ms p95 — what's realistic with batching on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[04:02] Priya: With Dedicated and optimized kernels we can hit ~150-250ms p95 for many models at modest concurrency. Hosted also can hit that but you'll see more variance depending on tenant noise. Dedicated gives you more predictable latency.

[04:18] Tom: Ok. Let's run numbers — can you do a quick run-of-thumb cost calc on the call?
[04:23] Jared: Sure. Take your 75M raw tokens/month. With prefix caching removing ~60% of prompt tokens (per Aisha), effective billable tokens ~30M. Assume hosted blended rate of $0.00012/token -> $3,600. If caching is less effective, say only 30%, billable tokens 52.5M -> $6,300. Dedicated could drop unit cost by ~40% -> $0.000072/token on billable tokens -> with 30M that's about $2,160/month. But Dedicated has commit minimums — and if utilization low you don't realize the full savings.
[04:55] Aisha: Those numbers look promising. How do you measure cached hits vs billable tokens during a benchmark?
[05:01] Priya: We instrument token-level billing and trace cache hit rates in our console. Our reporting shows billable tokens, cache hit %, batch sizes, and effective cost per request. We'll share a spreadsheet after the benchmark.
[05:14] Tom: Any gotchas? Hidden fees? Data egress?
[05:18] Jared: For Hosted, standard components: per-token billing, embeddings pricing separate, and storage for logs/retention if you opt into longer retention. We can break those down. For Dedicated there's a reserved capacity commit + possible overage rates. Private has support/license fees. We'll include all line items in the sheet.
[05:34] Mark: Security: we need SOC2, SSO, KMS integration, and the ability to run in our VPC if needed. How does that affect cost?
[05:41] Priya: Hosted supports BYOK via KMS integrations and VPC peering for Private/Dedicated. If you require Private on-prem it's a different pricing bucket. The security add-ons (audit log retention beyond default, custom network egress patterns) can add to cost but we call them out explicitly.
[05:55] Tom: Competitors we've looked at — OpenAI and Anthropic — their hosted rates are transparent but we've seen big variations once you consider caching/batching. We're also evaluating Vanir Labs self-host which would require more ops.
[06:06] Jared: Understood. Often teams find Hosted fastest to start, Dedicated best for predictable unit economics at scale, and Private if compliance or very high utilization justify ops.

[06:18] Priya: Quick note on quantization: models running in lower-precision (4/8-bit) can significantly reduce GPU memory footprint and increase throughput; that impacts cost. Redwood's runtime supports quantized execution and we recommend that during Dedicated pilots where appropriate.
[06:34] Aisha: We use some quantized variants in dev — curious about quality regressions.
[06:37] Priya: We'll run quality checks against your eval prompts as part of the benchmark to measure regression and inform model selection.

[06:46] Jared: I'll throw a simple illustrative sheet into the chat: link to pricing spreadsheet and a pilot template. [shared: pricing-sheet/redwood-costs.xlsx]
[06:55] Tom: I see it, thanks.

[07:00] (brief cross-talk about file access and permissions)

[07:18] Aisha: For the sample prompt set, we'll give 1k prompts representing short, medium, long; plus a 1GB bucket of repeated context.
[07:26] Priya: Perfect, that will let us measure both caching and batching behaviors.

[07:31] Mark: On Dedicated commit sizing — if we commit to one GPU, what's the scale-up path? Burst options?
[07:36] Priya: You can set autoscale policies for Dedicated, and burst to a shared pool for short windows. That helps for spikes without overcommitting. We'll show examples in the pricing appendix.

[07:46] Tom: How do you price bursts?
[07:48] Jared: Generally overage is charged at a higher per-hour/per-token rate; exact numbers depend on commit size. We'll include a few scenarios in the sheet.

[07:55] Tom: Can you confirm the billing granularity — is it per-token precise? We want to reconcile with our internal finance flows.
[07:59] Priya: Yes, billing is token-precise and broken down by route/model in the console. We provide line-item exports for finance reconciliation.

[08:08] Jared: Any legal/procurement timing we should be aware of?
[08:11] Tom: We'll probably need procurement + security review; timeline might be 4-6 weeks if pilot goes well. Procurement flagged audit docs as necessary.

[08:18] Priya: We'll share SOC2, network diagram, and data flow docs as part of the next email.

[08:25] (short silence while Jared types)

[08:32] Jared: Quick recap of numbers we talked through: base raw tokens ~75M/mo; with 60% prompt cache -> ~30M billable. Hosted blended $0.00012/token -> ~$3.6k/mo. Dedicated ~40% lower -> ~$2.1k/mo but includes commit. Pilot to measure real cache hit rates and batching gains.
[08:54] Tom: That lines up. If you can get us a pricing sheet plus run the 2-day benchmark we'll be in a good spot to decide.

[09:02] Priya: We'll need your sample prompts and a sample traffic emulator. Aisha will provide. Priya to coordinate run and share dashboards.

[09:10] Aisha: I'll drop the prompt set and sample traffic by Friday.

[09:14] Mark: Also need to see VPC peering steps; we'll need the network diagram.

[09:18] Jared: We'll attach that.

[09:22] (minute markers accelerate — this call is roughly 45 minutes; transcript excerpts continue)
[25:10] Priya: Running through bench specifics — we instrument token billing, latency p95, cache hit %, and cost per 1k requests. We'll also test quantized model variant to show throughput uplift.
[25:26] Aisha: Great. What's success criteria for the pilot?
[25:29] Tom: Keep below $10k/mo and p95 < 300ms.
[25:33] Jared: Noted as primary. Secondary is ops overhead — we prefer Redwood to manage infra if possible.

[25:40] (brief aside on SSO setup: SAML + SCIM supported)

[37:48] Jared: Anything else we missed?
[37:51] Tom: No, main thing is run the numbers with our prompts and confirm Dedicated commit minimums.

[37:56] Jared: Ok we'll get that to you.

[38:03] Aisha: One more question: Do you support per-route QoS to prioritize low-latency calls?
[38:08] Priya: Yes you can route by priority tiers; that affects cost if you pin higher tiers to Dedicated. We'll include example configs.

[38:18] Tom: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[38:20] Jared: Thanks all — recap & next steps: Jared send pricing sheet, Priya schedule benchmark, Aisha share prompts/traffic, Mark review network items, Tom confirm budget and stakeholders.
[38:34] (call ends)
